x.around: During the day, in the central areas, you can move easily even on foot. At dusk, it is recommended for tourists not to venture alone on foot.

hidden.d: Opened in 1896 and rebuilt in 2006 after an earthquake, this has a capacity of 20,000. It hosts the combined Windies Test team, the Trinidad & Tobago island team, and Trinbago Knight Riders in the T20 Caribbean Premier League.

Opened at the end of 2009, the construction of this building led to numerous allegations of corruption. The design is supposed to represent Trinidad's national flower but it has been much criticised as being out of keeping with…
A large park in the middle of the city. It has a circumference of 3.5 km and is a popular spot around sunset for joggers and walkers.
Built in 1902 by a wealthy merchant, Mr. William Gordon, this house features a veranda made of white marble, hand hewn yellow limestone bricks, and a staircase constructed from wood from Guyana.

A major skyscraper development designed to revitalise the city's waterfront with the Hyatt Regency Trinidad at its heart. This is the only section of Port of Spain's waterfront which is accessible to the public.

n.es: Centro Costero Internacional de Puerto España

hidden.d: Established in 1818, these are one of the oldest gardens in the Caribbean. 700 trees of which 13% are indigenous to Trinidad and Tobago.

x.intro: Port of Spain, on the northwest coast of Trinidad island, is the capital city of Trinidad and Tobago. The city is famous for its carnival, second only to that of Rio in importance but preferred by many because of its perceptions of being safer. A bustling and friendly city, Port of Spain is a great place to spend a couple of days and is the hub for the Trinidad's famous carnival.

must.d: This is the National Museum and Art Gallery of Trinidad and Tobago. Founded in 1892, this striking colonial building houses an extensive collection of artifacts and antiques from throughout Trinidad's history.
This swamp is a must-see for bird watchers. Several indigenous species of bird nest in the bird sanctuary, including one of the national birds, the Scarlet Ibis (Eudocimus ruber).
Trinidad and Tobago's only zoo, features a wide variety of tropical species including lions, tigers, monkeys, birds and fish. It is in the capital, Port of Spain.

x.safe: Trinidad has one of the highest murder rates in the world. Tourists are less affected by this. If you are sensible and stick to the main areas, you shouldn't have a problem and will find the locals incredibly friendly. Avoid any ostentatious display of wealth, and don't wander down dark backstreets at night or on your own.

cities.d: birthplace of famous calypso artiste "Lord Kitchener"

x.around: There are many taxi and maxi taxi stops in Arima, but there is also public transportation provided by the Government. The Public Transport Service Company (PTSC) runs many bus services throughout the town. The main bus depot is the PTSC Terminal Bus Stop on Pro Queen Street.

hidden.d: A birdwatching centre of the world. There are cottages to stay in, but one doesn't need to be an overnight guest to visit.

x.intro: Arima is one of 3 Boroughs in Trinidad. Its name is derived from the Arawak language, and it means "water".

cities.d: fastest growing and largest municipality mostly populated by descendants of East Indian indentured labourers

hidden.d: A clean and relaxing spa. They provide a complimentary cheesecake and tea/coffee at the end of your session.

An annual exposition Indo-Trinidadian culture in the period leading up Diwali around October or November. The village of Felicity, on the western end of Chaguanas, is famous for its elaborate Diwali celebrations.

x.intro: Chaguanas is a city in central Trinidad, split almost halfway between the country's two other major cities Port of Spain and San Fernando. Chaguanas is a drawcard for Indo-Trinidadian culture, with the city sparking into life during various festivals throughout the year.

cities.d: area in northwest Trinidad that is the yachting centre of the country with many facilities for boat owners

x.intro: Chaguaramas is a port and peninsular in the northwestern Trinidad.

cities.d: south western municipality, which lies on the outskirts of the La Brea Pitch Lake and is known for oil production

x.intro: Point Fortin (or just "Point") is the main town in the lightly populated deep south peninsula of Trinidad. It is not far from the city of San Fernando, it is the gateway to the rich treasure of coastline on both the Gulf of Paria and the Atlantic. Point is pretty much the last business area you would find going to the south of Trinidad.

x.around: Getting around on the island is very simple. There are mini vans for hire called Maxi Taxis, which carry passengers from various towns.

hidden.d: A wetland habitat that is home to locally endangered wetland birds. The Trust's setting is unlikely, near an industrial area of the state-owned Petrotrin oil refinery, with flames spouting from flare stacks in the sky.

x.intro: San Fernando is Trinidad's busy second city. It is built on hills including the most famous in Trinidad -- San Fernando Hill. San Fernando is very much a carnival city, experiencing a full build-up to its own wide assortment of competitions in Skinner Park as well as energetic parades. It is also known for the Pointe-a-Pierre Wild Fowl Trust near an oil refinery to the north of the San Fernando.

x.around: A local taxi to Black Rock will cost around TT$10 but expect TT$100 or more at Castries street.
x.intro: Scarborough is the main city on the island of Tobago, part of Trinidad and Tobago, a Caribbean country.

next.d: the inter-island ferry operates a daily (but limited) ferry service for TT$50 to the other island.

intro: Trinidad and Tobago (TT) is a nation consisting primarily of two Caribbean islands, Trinidad and Tobago, just off the northeastern coast of Venezuela. The country is the most industrialised and one of the most prosperous in the Caribbean. Overall, tourism is not a major industry (though the island of Tobago has proportionally more), leaving the islands replete with natural unspoiled beauty not found in most other Caribbean countries.
